production.note: US model years. Start: BMW NA's press kit is titled '2006 BMW Z4 M Coupe' (dated April 19, 2006), and BMW's March 2006 release announces the North American debut (bmw-us-m-coupe-debut). End: Consumer Guide's 2003-08 Z4 review lists the M coupe through 2008, the Z4's final year on that platform (cg-z4-2003-08).

body.note: The M Roadster is sold as its own model and is not covered by this record.

configuration.note: 'The M coupe will feature the 330 horsepower, 3.2-liter inline six-cylinder engine' (S54)

displacementL.note: '3.2-liter inline six-cylinder engine'. No opened page gave the cc figure (the S54 engine).

aspiration.note: Inferred: KBB lists the engine as '6-Cyl, 3.2 Liter' with no turbocharger or supercharger, and no opened source mentions forced induction.

transmission.note: 'this engine works through a six-speed manual transmission'. Manual only: Consumer Guide lists no automatic for the M (cg-z4-2003-08), and the six-speed STEPTRONIC automatic was offered on the Z4 Coupe 3.0si, not the M.

powerHp.note: Quote (BMW of North America press release): "The M coupe will feature the 330 horsepower, 3.2-liter inline six-cylinder engine". KBB's 2008 page agrees: "330 @ 7900 RPM" (kbb-2008-z4m-coupe). The rating was unchanged for 2006-2008 (Consumer Guide's engine table lists 330 hp for the generation, cg-z4-2003-08).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database plus a single article). 6-speed manual. Quote (KBB, 2008 Z4 M Coupe): "3230 lbs." curb weight. MotoringFile (Gabriel Bridger) gives the same figure against the M3: 'Less weight (3230lbs)' (motoringfile-z4m-coupe). No BMW NA curb weight could be opened: the press kit's specification attachments would not load as text. See discrepancies for auto123's figure. KBB's page is the 2008 model year; MotoringFile's April 2007 review ties the same 3,230 lb to the reference year, and Consumer Guide lists no spec changes over 2006-2008.

discrepancies.reason: Auto123's pre-launch Canadian preview prints '1,415 kg (3120 lbs)', a metric (European-style kerb) figure from January 2006; KBB and MotoringFile give 3,230 lb for the US car.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 3,230 lb: the two US-market sources agree exactly, and auto123's kg-based preview figure predates the car's North American launch.

provisionalNote: Weight (3,230 lb) rests on KBB (database) and a single MotoringFile article, agreeing. Power (330 hp) is fully sourced from BMW NA's press release. A BMW NA specification sheet (the press kit's attachments, which would not open as text) or a major magazine spec panel would replace the weight.
